title: Beauty's Undisputed Heavyweights: How Dove and Vaseline Are Fueling Unilever's Ascent
summary: Unilever reported robust first-half sales nearing 25.6 billion euros, with growth accelerating significantly in the second quarter. This impressive performance was largely spearheaded by its enduring beauty 'power brands' like Dove, Sunsilk, and Vaseline, demonstrating the resilience and strategic value of established consumer favorites.
content:
Unilever, the sprawling consumer goods titan, has reported a remarkably strong first half of the year, defying market headwinds to post a nearly 5 percent rise in underlying sales, reaching a robust 25.6 billion euros. What's truly compelling is the engine behind this accelerating growth, particularly in the second quarter: not flashy new tech, but the enduring power of its beloved beauty brands.

Leading the charge were familiar names like Dove, Sunsilk, and Vaseline, each delivering double-digit growth. These aren't just legacy products; they represent deeply entrenched consumer trust and innovative brand management. In an era where fragmented markets and fleeting trends often dominate headlines, these 'power brands' illustrate the enduring value of established quality and global reach. Their consistent performance underscores a strategic win for Unilever, proving that investing in and refreshing tried-and-true brands can yield significant returns.

This surge, particularly in the beauty segment, paints a picture of a company successfully navigating a complex economic landscape. While Unilever's portfolio spans everything from food to home care, the stellar performance of its personal care division highlights where consumer spending remains resilient and where brand loyalty translates directly into financial uplift. It suggests that, even amidst inflationary pressures, consumers are willing to invest in personal care essentials and trusted brands that deliver perceived value and consistent quality. This impressive showing sets a promising trajectory for the latter half of the year, signaling Unilever's strategic focus on these resilient categories is paying dividends.
keyTakeaways: Unilever achieved strong financial results in the first half, with underlying sales up nearly 5% to 25.6 billion euros.
Growth was significantly driven by 'power brands' in the beauty segment, including Dove, Sunsilk, and Vaseline, which all saw double-digit increases.
The performance highlights the enduring strength and strategic importance of established consumer brands in a challenging economic climate.
author: Samantha Conti

title: Mininglamp Technology Ignites Global AI Challenge for the Future of Web Data
summary: Mininglamp Technology has officially launched the WebRetriever Global Challenge, inviting top innovators to advance AI-powered web information retrieval. The competition, co-organized by Peking University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, offers a $15,000 prize pool to drive breakthroughs in intelligent data extraction.
content:
Beijing-based AI powerhouse Mininglamp Technology has officially thrown down the gauntlet, launching its WebRetriever Global Challenge. With registrations now open, the competition invites top minds from around the world to tackle the intricate art of advanced web information extraction, all vying for a share of a compelling $15,000 prize pool. It’s a clear signal that the company, a significant player in enterprise-level AI and knowledge graphs, is doubling down on innovation to solve one of the internet's most persistent headaches: making sense of its vast, unstructured data.

In an age drowning in digital information, the ability to accurately and efficiently retrieve, process, and structure data from the sprawling web is more critical than ever. The WebRetriever Challenge isn't just about scraping; it’s a sophisticated test for intelligent agents capable of understanding context, extracting nuanced insights, and building robust knowledge bases from diverse online sources. Such breakthroughs are pivotal for everything from next-gen intelligent search to sophisticated business intelligence and automated decision-making, addressing the ever-growing challenge of information overload.

Co-organized with prestigious academic powerhouses like Peking University and the Institute of Automation of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the challenge signals a serious commitment to fostering next-generation AI talent and pushing cutting-edge research. For developers, data scientists, and AI enthusiasts worldwide, it’s an opportunity not just to showcase their skills on a truly global stage, but to directly contribute to the foundational technologies that will underpin tomorrow's most intelligent systems. With registration officially open as of July 28, 2026, the race is on for innovators ready to redefine how we interact with the web’s boundless information.
keyTakeaways: Mininglamp Technology has launched the WebRetriever Global Challenge to advance AI-powered web information retrieval.
The competition offers a $15,000 prize pool and is co-organized with Peking University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
It aims to attract global talent to innovate in intelligent data extraction, critical for future AI systems and knowledge graphs.
author: Staff Writer

title: India's Tech Revolution: Engineers, Not Just Coders, Are the New High Earners
summary: India's tech job market is undergoing a significant transformation, with roles in AI, semiconductor manufacturing, and infrastructure now seeing stronger salary growth than traditional software development. This shift, driven by ambitious government initiatives and emerging technologies, signals a new era for the nation's talent landscape.
content:
For nearly two decades, the glittering promise of a high-flying career in India almost exclusively pointed towards software development. The nation built its global reputation, and countless fortunes, on the backs of brilliant coders churning out everything from enterprise solutions to consumer apps.

But that long-held dynamic is experiencing a dramatic recalibration. A new report from TeamLease reveals a compelling trend: India's burgeoning focus on artificial intelligence, semiconductor manufacturing, and electric vehicles is creating a fresh hierarchy of high-paying jobs. Suddenly, it's the engineers specializing in AI, the technical support wizards, and the infrastructure professionals who are commanding more robust salary growth, eclipsing their software development counterparts.

This pivot isn't happening in a vacuum. It's a direct consequence of India's ambitious governmental push to become a global hub for advanced manufacturing and deep tech. Massive investments in semiconductor fabrication, along with a fervent embrace of AI and the burgeoning EV market, are rapidly reshaping the demand for skilled talent. These sectors require a different breed of expertise – one focused on hardware integration, complex system design, and the intricate dance of physical and digital infrastructure.

What this signifies is a maturation of India's tech story. It's moving beyond a primary reliance on IT services and into a more diversified, value-added technology ecosystem. For aspiring professionals, the message is clear: while coding remains vital, the most lucrative opportunities are increasingly found at the intersection of software, hardware, and advanced manufacturing, ushering in a thrilling new chapter for India's economic prowess.
keyTakeaways: India's job market is shifting, with engineers in AI, semiconductors, and EVs now seeing greater salary growth than traditional software developers.
This transformation is driven by significant government investments and national pushes into advanced manufacturing and deep technology sectors.
The change signals India's strategic move towards a diversified, high-value technology economy beyond just IT services.
author: ET Online
